newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares edge up, Reliance leads the way.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares edge up, Reliance leads the way.

text.p: Delhi shares drifted higher in early trade on Tuesday and Reliance Industries continued to attract buyers, brokers said.
At the end of 30 minutes of trade, the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index was up 1.17 points at 803.66.
"The market has been showing gradual recovery trends. The recovery is likely to extend to B-group stocks," said B.K. Nagpal of brokerage house B.B. Portfolio.
Reliance, which bucked the market's trend on Monday to gain five rupees, added one rupee to 311.4 rupees. Brokers said speculation that the firm might announce a bonus issue spurred buying.
Traders said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and other players made fresh purchases in Hindustan Lever, State Bank of India and Nestle India.
Domestic financial institutions remained on the sidelines, they said.
State Bank of India edged up 0.50 rupee to 314.75. Hindustan Lever, which fell sharply on Monday, rebounded eight rupees to 1,212 on FII buying.
Nestle India gained two rupees to 266.
Larsen and Toubro rose one rupee to 221.25.
